title: {Syn} SHA-256 Makes Small Changes Avalanche
content:
SHA-256 maps input data to a 256-bit digest. A tiny input change should produce an unrelated-looking output, a behavior called the avalanche effect.

Cryptographic hashes are not encryption. They are one-way fingerprints used for integrity checks, commitments, proof-of-work systems, and signatures.

Why it matters: cryptography keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
